hero.headline: Build The Strength That Keeps Pain From Coming Back.
hero.subheadline: Starke Physiotherapy Clinic in Porur treats injuries and chronic pain with structured strength-based rehabilitation — built for people who sit at a desk all day and want a body that can actually keep up outside of it.

about.title: Recovery that makes you stronger than before
body: Starke Physiotherapy Clinic was started around a simple observation: most pain that brings people into a clinic in Porur isn't from a dramatic injury — it's from years of poor posture, weak stabilizing muscles, and bodies that were never rebuilt with real strength after the last time something hurt. We treat the injury in front of us, but we don't stop there.

Every plan combines hands-on assessment with progressive strength training, so patients leave not just pain-free but genuinely more resilient — whether that means a desk job that no longer wrecks your lower back, or a body that can handle real physical activity without breaking down again.
highlights: Strength-based recovery plans, not just passive treatment
Dedicated posture and ergonomic assessment for desk-job pain
Modern strength and rehab equipment on-site
Injury prevention built into every recovery plan

services.name: Posture & Ergonomic Assessment
services.tagline: Find out what your desk is actually doing to your body
services.overview: We assess how you sit, stand, and move through a typical workday, then identify the specific postural habits and ergonomic gaps driving your pain — and fix them, not just treat the symptom.
symptoms: Pain that consistently worsens by the end of a workday
Rounded shoulders or forward head posture
Stiffness after long periods at a desk
benefits: Identifies the actual cause of desk-related pain
Reduces recurrence, not just today's discomfort
services.recovery: Most patients notice reduced discomfort within 3–4 weeks of consistent corrective exercise.

faqs.question: Do I need to bring anything from my office setup?
faqs.answer: Photos of your desk and chair setup are helpful but not required — we can work from a description of your daily routine.

services.name: Strength-Based Rehabilitation
services.tagline: Recovery that leaves you stronger than before the injury
services.overview: Rather than stopping at pain relief, our strength-based rehab programs progressively rebuild the muscles and stability around an injury so you're less likely to end up back here in six months.
symptoms: Difficulty returning to normal activity levels
benefits: Builds resilience, not just short-term relief
Progress tracked against clear strength benchmarks
services.recovery: Typical strength-rebuilding programs run 6–10 weeks, with progress reviewed every two weeks.

services.name: Chronic Pain Management
services.tagline: A structured plan for pain that hasn't responded to rest
services.overview: For pain that has lingered for months, we build a structured management plan combining hands-on therapy, targeted strengthening, and realistic activity pacing to reduce pain and restore function over time.
symptoms: Pain that limits daily activity or sleep
Previous treatments that gave only short-term relief
benefits: Addresses long-standing pain, not just recent flare-ups
Reduces reliance on repeated short-term fixes
services.recovery: Chronic pain programs are typically reviewed monthly, with most patients reporting meaningful improvement by week 8.

services.name: Pre/Post-Workout Injury Prevention
services.overview: For gym-goers and active adults, we assess movement patterns and muscle imbalances before they become injuries, and build a pre- and post-workout routine that keeps you training consistently.
symptoms: Recurring niggles during or after training
Muscle tightness or imbalance noticed during workouts
History of the same injury flaring up repeatedly
benefits: Fewer training interruptions from recurring injuries
Routines that fit around your actual training schedule

services.name: Neck & Back Pain Therapy
services.tagline: Relief that holds up once you're back at your desk
services.overview: Neck and back pain rarely comes from a single cause — we treat the immediate pain with hands-on therapy while correcting the postural and strength deficits that keep bringing it back.
symptoms: Persistent neck or lower back pain
Pain that worsens with prolonged sitting
Stiffness or reduced flexibility through the spine
benefits: Addresses the root cause, not just the pain flare-up
Long-term relief instead of repeat short-term treatment
services.recovery: Most patients see meaningful improvement within 4–6 weeks of consistent therapy.

faqs.question: Do I need an appointment or can I walk in?
faqs.answer: Walk-ins are welcome, but booking an appointment in advance helps us keep wait times short and ensures the right therapist is available for your condition.

faqs.question: What should I expect at my first session?
faqs.answer: Your first session includes a detailed assessment of your movement, posture, and pain history, followed by a discussion of a recommended treatment plan before any hands-on therapy begins.

faqs.question: What payment methods do you accept?
faqs.answer: We accept cash, UPI, and major cards. Payment is due at the time of each session unless other arrangements have been made.

faqs.question: How many sessions will I typically need?
faqs.answer: It varies by condition, but most patients complete a program of 6–10 sessions, with progress reviewed regularly to adjust the plan as needed.

faqs.question: Do you treat back pain caused by desk jobs?
faqs.answer: Yes — desk-job related back and neck pain is one of the most common conditions we treat, and our posture and ergonomic assessment is built specifically for it.

blogPosts.title: Why Sitting All Day Causes More Back Pain Than You Think
blogPosts.excerpt: It's not just posture — prolonged sitting weakens the exact muscles your back relies on to protect itself, and that's the part most advice misses.
blogPosts.author: Meera Krishnan
content: Most advice about desk-related back pain stops at "sit up straight," but posture is only part of the story — hours of sitting also switches off the glutes and deep core muscles that normally support your lower back.

When those stabilizing muscles go quiet for eight hours a day, your spine ends up absorbing load it was never meant to handle alone, which is why pain often shows up even in people who sit reasonably upright.
This is why stretching alone rarely fixes desk-related back pain for good — the muscles that switched off need to be actively retrained and strengthened, not just loosened.

A combination of ergonomic adjustments, movement breaks through the day, and a targeted strengthening routine addresses both the posture and the underlying weakness, which is the only approach that tends to hold up over time.
